title: Mitar Pyare and the Malerkotla Pathan

blocks.text: The Guru asks why certain tyrants were left alive, and a Sikh answers by recalling the role of a Malerkotla Pathan whose conduct stood apart from the worst of the crime. (10–12)
From that emotional ground the composition moves into the famous shabad Mitar Pyare, where longing, separation, pain, and steadfastness are given lyrical form instead of bare chronicle. (13–14)
The page then resumes the story at Dina and nearby settlements, where shelter, food, and small acts of support continue even under the shadow of catastrophe. (15–16)
